title: Build the project from the draft
request: When the user says 'Let's build the solution', the draft becomes a project with everything the chat and the wizard established, and the solution enters the project through the workflow validator.
spec: POST /api/drafts/{id}/build: a project with the cleaned table, the solution, the settings, the pack, the workflow and what the chat established; the solution saved through the workflow validator. Done when the sample-then-build flow test passes and a draft without data builds a plan-only project.
plan: Create the project, copy the cleaned Parquet file and attach it.
Carry over the synthetic flag, the settings (rows, quick mode, folds) and the budget; keep a copy of the pack, workflow, cleaning log and answers.
Save the solution through studio.graph.check and graph.log so the transition log starts with an allowed set_solution.
Make building twice return the same project.
Let a draft with no data build a plan the user can add data to later.

decisions.decision: The solution goes through the same graph check as any later edit.
decisions.why: A project must never start in a state the validator would refuse.
A double click or a retried request must not create two projects.

change: build_project in dclab_rnd/draft/api.py creating the project from the draft, logging the solution as a set_solution move.

findings.defect: The transition log recorded the state after the move instead of before it.
findings.scenario: Building from a draft logged set_solution with the state after the move, while the project page's own rows record the state before the move; a built project's first row would not have matched how the page reads its log.
findings.cause: The order of logging and applying was swapped.
findings.fix: Record the state before the move, as the project page expects.
findings.impact: A built project's first log row would have shown the solution already set before set_solution ran. The Workflow page's replay of the log would start from the wrong state, and the record of the first move would not match what happened.

findings.defect: The notebook exported from a project built on Home failed on its first cell, because it read the project's Parquet file with pd.read_csv.
findings.scenario: Running the synthetic flow end to end and opening the exports: the project built from the draft holds its table as clean.parquet, and the notebook's data cell called pd.read_csv on that file, which cannot parse Parquet, so the notebook stopped at its first code cell.
findings.cause: The exporter was written when every project's table was an uploaded CSV and always emitted pd.read_csv; building from a draft introduced Parquet files the exporter did not know about.
findings.fix: The exporter writes the read call by the file's type, the same way data.load_table reads it: read_parquet for .parquet, read_csv with a tab separator for .tsv, read_excel for Excel, read_json for .json, read_csv otherwise.
findings.test: tests/test_studio.py export checks: a project whose file is sim.parquet exports frame = pd.read_parquet('sim.parquet'), and a .tsv file gets the tab separator.
findings.impact: Every project created from Home, uploads, studied samples and synthetic data alike, exported a notebook that could not run. The notebook is the artefact meant to let a reviewer reproduce the run, so the reproduction failed before any number could be checked.
findings.open: The exporter and data.load_table each keep their own list of file types; a type added to one and not the other would fail the same way.

outcome: Done: a draft builds a project (or a plan-only project without data) whose log starts with an allowed set_solution.
lessons: When two components share a log, write down what each row means (state before or after) and test it from the reader's side.
risks: A project starts in a state the workflow validator would refuse, because the solution bypassed the graph check.
A double click or a retried request creates two projects from one draft.
The synthetic flag, the settings or the cleaned file's types are lost between the draft and the project.
The transition log's first row does not mean what the project page assumes it means.
A draft without data cannot build at all, though the user wants to plan first.
